newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes easier, seen testing support.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes easier, seen testing support.

text.p: Bullion prices fixed easier on Thursday and although dealers forecast a move lower to test support, they expected a bounce higher after that.
"There is decent volume and two way business in what feels like a $342-$347 range. There is the chance of a break-out," one dealer said.
Gold was fixed at $344.85 per ounce down from $346.25 on Wednesday after encountering selling against a higher yen and some producer selling in the Far East.
The death of Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping had no impact on gold prices in Europe, dealers said.
"There is a chance that gold will test demand under the market and put on a bounce from there," one dealer said. "The risk today is still to the upside," he added.
A weaker dollar was helping gold sustain current levels against ongoing pressure from accelerated selling by producers, fund selling and the threat of sales from central bank reserves.
Dealers said physical demand remained stong and supportive although the negative factors were more significant.
Silver opened unchanged in Europe at $5.18/$5.20 but edged back a couple of cents in a quiet market which was beginning to look slightly overbought.

"Technically silver could retrace to $5.05-$5.12 and if that holds we could see a good bounce," a dealer said, forecasting a spike up to possibly new highs around $5.40. Platinum and palladium were easier too reflecting selling in Tokyo against a stronger yen.
Some dealers dismissed the news that the U.S. Government would sell small quantities of platinum and palladium from its strategic stockpile on March 24 as a significant factor.
"Norilsk and Russia are still the major factors," a dealer said. Platinum was indicated at $363.50/$364.50 down $3.50 and palladium was up $.25 at $133.00/$134.00.
